title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
abstract: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.
summary: This paper introduces a novel theory to describe the partial indistinguishability of identical particles possessing internal, invariant degrees of freedom. It defines quantitative measures, such as the indistinguishability function and projective measures, that characterize how close the system is to ideal bosonic or fermionic behavior. The results provide experimentally testable bounds on indistinguishability using marginal measurements.
main_problem: The paper develops a comprehensive theory to quantify the partial indistinguishability of identical particles when their degrees of freedom are partitioned into visible (unitarily evolving) and internal (dynamically invariant) parts.
main_result: The indistinguishability is characterized by an 'indistinguishability function' and is quantified by projective measures, which yield a hierarchy of upper bounds on the observable indistinguishability.
method: The authors use first-quantization and second-quantization formalisms, employing symmetry projectors (related to the symmetric group) to decompose the state and define various indistinguishability measures.
model_or_system: The model consists of $n$ identical bosons or fermions whose single-particle Hilbert space is split into visible and internal degrees of freedom. The evolution is restricted to unitary transformations acting only on the visible part.
key_observables: Indistinguishability Measure $D(\hat{\varrho})$, Emulation Measure $eD(\hat{\varrho})$, and the Projective Measure $D_n$ on the symmetry spectrum.
important_parameters: The number of particles ($n$), the structure of the symmetry group ($S_n$), and the parameters defining the visible state $\hat{\varrho}(	ext{vis})$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a suitable family of interferometers for reconstruction and relies on the structure of unitary linear evolutions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the core indistinguishability measures, deriving the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, and finally establishing the hierarchy of upper bounds using marginal projective measures.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for quantifying quantum indistinguishability beyond the standard Bose/Fermi statistics, which is crucial for understanding multi-particle quantum interference in optics and quantum simulation.
